dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt system (日医標準レセプトソフト); GnuCOBOL-based open-source Japanese medical billing platform
evidence: COPY CPSYSKANRI.INC / CPSK1001.INC / MCPDATA.INC / MCPAREA etc.

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical inpatient billing/receipt processing; specifically handles food-service charge assignment target acquisition for psychiatric long-term hospitalization (Heisei 28 revision)
purpose.summary: This subprogram (ORCSSKJKEEP) is part of the JMA ORCA standard medical receipt software. It retrieves and evaluates inpatient accounting records to determine applicable food/nutrition charge targets for psychiatric ward long-term hospitalization cases, including checks for rare disease (nanbyo) and pediatric specific disease public expense codes, and handles the Heisei 28 (2016) revision logic.

notable_features: 21 COPY statements for shared record layouts (CPNYUINACCT, CPPTINF, CPHKNCOMBI, etc.)
LINKAGE SECTION with SPA (scratchpad area) pattern typical of ORCA
CALL to ORCSDAY date utility subprogram
PERFORM VARYING loops over 31-day arrays for daily hospitalization accounting
REDEFINES clauses for date field decomposition
OCCURS tables for insurance combination and rare-disease exclusion lists
Japanese EUC-JP encoded comments (latin-1 decoded as mojibake)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS; uses MCP (middleware) table access pattern
verdict.notes: File decoded as latin-1 but comments are actually EUC-JP Japanese text, appearing as mojibake. Source is truncated at 16000 chars out of 78211 bytes (1719 lines total). The MCP-TABLE/MCP-PATHNAME pattern is the ORCA middleware database access mechanism, not standard COBOL file I/O. Program is a subprogram called by the inpatient receipt calculation subsystem.
